page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.tiny is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the shared instance family. The server provides a minimal resource footprint consisting of 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to a single physical core on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. System memory is sized at 1.0 GB RAM, matching a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results reflect the constrained single-core and low-memory environment. The instance scored 1087.59 in stress-ng for both single-core and multi-core operations, ranking in the lower tiers across comparative benchmarks. In PassMark testing, the server attained a CPU score of 1316.17 and a memory score of 690.99. Memory throughput reached 8.5 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 7.1 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics demonstrate an output of 1.43 million operations per second for Redis SET workloads and 0.93 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.n1.tiny offers low computational overhead suitable for minimal infrastructure baselines. The trade-off is bounded throughput, absence of integrated storage, and limited RAM, which introduces risks of memory exhaustion under multi-process loads. Consequently, this server type is suitable for non-critical lightweight tasks, basic testing environments, small automated scripts, proxy nodes, or lightweight background workers that do not require extensive parallel processing or large working sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.tiny is an entry-tier virtual server from the shared family featuring 1 vCPU and 1.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it provides dedicated core allocation with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. The configuration includes no integrated local storage or graphics accelerators, necessitating remote block storage for data persistence. Across benchmark suites, the server shows modest throughput, recording 1087.59 in stress-ng single-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 1316.17, and 1.43 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Due to strict CPU and memory limits, the instance delivers a low-cost profile balanced against minimal performance headroom. It is appropriate for non-demanding tasks, small proxy servers, light web utilities, simple scripts, and test-bed environments.
